jobs.title: Project Worker, Housing First, South East

description.html:
Project Worker, Housing First, South East

Location: Tipperary

Contract: Full Time, 1 Year Fixed Term
The Purpose of this role is to support people who are sleeping rough and/or experiencing long-term and multiple exclusion homelessness to move into secure, permanent housing at the earliest opportunity, without preconditions for sobriety or treatment compliance.

What you will do:

Making Contact

  • Engage with people sleeping rough and/or experiencing long-term or multiple exclusion homelessness in Kilkenny.

  • Work collaboratively with Outreach, Emergency Accommodation and other relevant services, including following up on referrals from the Homeless Action Team (HAT).

  • Explain the Housing First Service, available supports and how the model differs from other approaches.

  • Signpost to appropriate services and obtain consent for referrals, advocacy, record-keeping and information sharing.

Housing Assessment, Access & Allocation

  • Assess housing needs, priorities and risks using agreed assessment tools.

  • Support participants to access Local Authority housing, HAP/RAS and relevant social welfare entitlements.

  • Identify housing preferences, arrange viewings and support participants to make informed choices.

  • Liaise and advocate with Local Authorities, the Department of Social Protection, landlords and other relevant agencies.

  • Follow the Housing First approach, including housing without preconditions and supporting re-housing where tenancies break down.

Key Working, Support Plans & Case Management

  • Complete assessments, risk management plans and individual support plans based on each participant’s needs and choices.

  • Provide key-working support across areas including health, mental health, addiction, independent living, employment, education and relationships.

  • Coordinate with health, housing, social welfare and other agencies to ensure participants can access appropriate supports and entitlements.

  • Provide practical tenancy and independent living support through home visits, advocacy and skills development.

  • Work collaboratively with internal and external services, including case management and Homeless Action Team meetings where required.

Addressing Problems & Tenancy Breakdown

  • Ensure tenants understand their rights and responsibilities under the Residential Tenancies Act.

  • Identify issues that may threaten tenancy stability and coordinate appropriate support with tenants, landlords and relevant services.

  • Advocate for participants while maintaining positive relationships with landlords, neighbours and partner agencies.

  • Continue supporting participants following tenancy breakdown and work towards re-housing at the earliest opportunity.

Induction to Accommodation

  • Attend property viewings and support participants with their move into suitable accommodation.

  • Introduce tenants to their property and local amenities where required.

  • Explain tenancy agreements, accommodation details, rights and responsibilities.

  • Provide guidance on fire safety, health and safety, and the Housing First service model.

Accommodation

  • Advocate with external agencies to secure appropriate housing for participants.

  • Report property defects and support the timely completion of repairs.

  • Maintain positive relationships with landlords, property owners and housing providers.

  • Support tenants to maintain successful and sustainable tenancies.

Finance

  • Maintain accurate petty cash records and receipts.

  • Work with Housing Officers and relevant colleagues to address rent arrears or payment issues.

  • Ensure participants access appropriate benefits and financial entitlements.

Record Keeping

  • Maintain accurate, professional and up-to-date participant records, including PASS records.

  • Produce required statistics and reports for Focus Ireland and statutory agencies/funders.

  • Complete weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual reports as required.

  • Participate in project monitoring and evaluation.

Research & Service Improvement

  • Participate in relevant research, audits and quality improvement initiatives.

  • Contribute to service improvement plans arising from evaluation and audit findings.

  • Seek and incorporate service-user feedback into service development.

  • Remain flexible in responding to changing service needs and new initiatives.

Teamwork & Personal Development

  • Work collaboratively within the team while effectively managing an individual caseload.

  • Build strong working relationships with voluntary, statutory and interdisciplinary partner agencies.

  • Participate in team meetings, HAT meetings, working groups, planning days and supervision as required.

  • Engage in ongoing training, professional development and reflective practice.

  • Contribute to best practice and the overall objectives of Focus Ireland.

What you will need:

  • A third-level qualification at degree level in Social Care or a related area, such as Social Studies, Addiction Studies, Psychology, or similar, and/or be a CORU-registered Social Care Worker.

  • 2 years’ experience in residential social care services; preferably in the homeless sector.

  • leadership experience in social care services,including supervision of social care staff would be a distinct advantage.

  • Extensive experience in working with behaviours that may challenge and supporting care-staff in similar environments.

  • Supporting organisational change in a complex environment.

  • Recording, reporting and information management.

Focus Ireland is an equal opportunities employer

jobs.title: Social Care Worker, Dún Solas Templeogue, Dublin

description.html:
Social Care Worker, Dún Solas Templeogue, Dublin

Location: Dublin

Contract: Full Time, Permanent

The primary aim is to provide interventions necessary to address the young person’s issues and the issues preventing them from living at home. The aim is to provide a therapeutic care placement to the young people who most often present with emotional or behavioural difficulties and cannot live with their own families.

What you will do:

  • Work in line with Focus Ireland’s mission, values, policies, and procedures, contributing positively as part of the residential care team.

  • Support young people in a residential setting, promoting their safety, wellbeing, development, and positive outcomes.

  • Act as a Key Worker for designated young people, building effective relationships and coordinating supports with relevant external agencies.

  • Develop, implement, and review individual care plans and placement plans, ensuring accurate documentation and progress monitoring.

  • Provide trauma-informed support to young people, including those presenting with challenging behaviours and complex needs.

  • Advocate on behalf of young people in relation to social work, aftercare, education, training, health, legal, and other support services.

  • Promote the physical, emotional, social, cultural, and spiritual wellbeing, rights, and responsibilities of each young person.

  • Maintain positive engagement with families, social workers, and external stakeholders to support the needs and goals of young people.

  • Ensure all records, reports, and documentation are maintained in accordance with statutory, regulatory, safeguarding, and health and safety requirements.

  • Encourage and facilitate the participation of young people in decisions affecting their lives, both individually and within the wider service.

  • Attend and contribute to team meetings, reviews, training, and professional development activities, supporting continuous service improvement.

  • Comply with health and safety standards, undertake additional duties as required, and participate in a 24/7 seven-day roster system.

What you will need:

  • A Third Level qualification at degree level in the area of social care i.e. youth work, social studies, addiction, psychology etc and/or be a CORU registered Social Care Worker

  • Full clean driving license.

  • Proven direct work experience in a social care setting at a social care level or equivalent.

  • Experience of supporting marginalized clients/groups preferably adolescents.

  • A working knowledge and insight into the social issues (e.g. substance abuse) that affect young people, in particular young people, who have or are experiencing trauma and attachment issues.

  • Ability to manage and support young people in crisis who present with challenging behaviors based on the values and principles of best practice in Focus Ireland.

  • Working knowledge and understanding of Child Protection.

  • Working knowledge of the national standards for children’s residentials.

Focus Ireland is an equal opportunities employer
